candidates.title: Visual Asset Provenance Pipeline
candidates.why: The game has strong procedural canvas rendering, but no source-of-truth ledger for future Blender, generated, or downloaded visual assets. That makes a 3D art upgrade risky: assets can enter the repo without source files, export settings, license status, or runtime constraints. A small manifest plus source-folder contract turns every future visual improvement into an auditable pipeline instead of mystery media.
candidates.recipe: Create `assets/source/README.md` and `assets/visual-assets.json` documenting the 3D-authored sprite pipeline, allowed free/open sources, source/export paths, licensing, and optimization rules. Add `scripts/validate-visual-assets.mjs` plus an npm script so every manifest entry must include id, kind, sourceType, license, sourcePath, runtimePath, dimensions, and status.
candidates.evidence: `public/launch-assets/` contains exported launch SVG/PNG media and `scripts/generate-launch-assets.mjs`, but there is no `assets/source` folder, no visual asset manifest, and no validator. `docs/INTERNAL_TOOLS.md` is absent locally, so the internal-first choice is to build a repo-local manifest without adding dependencies.

L1.recipe: Add a markdown source-art contract and one JSON manifest entry for the current launch asset pack.

L2.recipe: Add manifest, source README, validator script, npm script, and entries for launch media plus runtime procedural sprites.

L3.recipe: Extend the validator to check image dimensions and warn when runtime assets exceed mobile texture budget.

candidates.title: Pseudo-3D Runtime Asset Primitives
candidates.why: Call of Doodie already renders enemies as shaded canvas forms, but the 3D-ish look is implicit inside one large renderer and the player still has hard-coded body/gun drawing. Extracting reusable porcelain/plastic/metal primitives lets the game look more authored today while leaving a clean swap point for Blender-rendered sprite sheets tomorrow. This improves readability and style coherence without making the whole game a fragile 3D migration.
candidates.recipe: Add `src/utils/visualPrimitives.js` with tested helpers for pseudo-3D tokens: material palette lookup, shaded orb/specular pass, and weapon barrel accent descriptors. Wire the player body and enemy body base in `drawGame.js` through those helpers while preserving existing telegraphs, hit flashes, labels, and emoji overlays.
candidates.evidence: `src/drawGame.js` already draws enemy body volume inline with inner depth ring/top-left highlight and hard-coded player helmet/vest/gun shapes. There is no reusable primitive module, so future sprite/3D swaps would require editing the monolithic renderer.

L1.recipe: Extract only shaded enemy body drawing into a pure helper and test material fallback.

L2.recipe: Extract enemy orb, player body, and weapon accent helpers; wire `drawGame.js`; add unit tests for palette/material contracts.

L3.recipe: Add an offscreen sprite-atlas cache keyed by enemy/player material so static shading is reused instead of repainted every frame.

candidates.title: Launch Media Asset Gate
candidates.why: The public manifest still points screenshot entries at SVG launch placeholders even though PNG generation exists. That is workable for browsers, but weak for store/listing workflows and gives no automated proof that launch media is present, sized, and tracked. A media gate makes the asset pipeline visible before every launch/closeout and creates the place to later require real gameplay screenshots.
candidates.recipe: Add `scripts/validate-launch-media.mjs` to verify every manifest screenshot has a generated PNG sibling and every launch PNG is represented in `assets/visual-assets.json`. Add `npm run launch:media-check` and update launch readiness documentation to treat real screenshot capture as the remaining human step.
candidates.evidence: `public/manifest.json` references five SVG screenshots; `scripts/generate-launch-assets.mjs` exports PNG siblings, but no script checks manifest-to-PNG parity or provenance coverage.

L1.recipe: Check that each manifest screenshot path has a PNG sibling in `public/launch-assets`.

L2.recipe: Also require each generated PNG to be tracked in the visual asset manifest and documented as placeholder or real screenshot.

L3.recipe: Use `sharp` metadata to verify exact screenshot dimensions and fail if wide/narrow form factors drift.

skipped.reason: Rejected on verification: current game is a tuned 2D canvas shooter with extensive input/replay tests. Full 3D migration would risk launch confidence; 3D-authored sprites are the safer first rung.
Deferred: live lookup did not verify the site, export terms, or license posture. Any use must pass package/source trust and rights provenance first.

executionLog.notes: Added `assets/source/README.md`, `assets/visual-assets.json`, `scripts/validate-visual-assets.mjs`, and `npm run assets:check`. Ark canon-update cargo queued to `vaultspark-studio-ops` for studio-wide per-game proprietary asset-library propagation. Verified with `npm run assets:check`.

Added `src/utils/visualPrimitives.js` and focused tests, then routed enemy body material shading plus player weapon/body/helmet drawing through reusable pseudo-3D primitives while preserving existing hit flashes, telegraphs, labels, and emoji overlays. Verified with focused tests, full `npm test` 503/503, build, and Playwright desktop/mobile canvas smoke.

Added `scripts/validate-launch-media.mjs` and `npm run launch:media-check` to require manifest screenshot PNG siblings and visual-asset provenance coverage. Also fixed Playwright e2e harness isolation by scoping testMatch and moving the dev server to strict port 53173. Verified with `npm run launch:media-check` and `npm run test:e2e` 2/2.
